summary: This is a Snowflake documentation page for the DROP APPLICATION ROLE command, which removes a specified application role from an application built with the Native App Framework. It gives the syntax (with optional IF EXISTS), describes the name parameter and its quoting and case-sensitivity rules, and lists usage notes. The notes say dropped roles cannot be recovered, must be recreated, and are not versioned, so a role should not be dropped while a running version depends on it. A single example drops the role APP_ROLE. The feature is noted as not supported on Google Cloud Platform.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the DROP APPLICATION ROLE command, which removes an application role from a Native App Framework application.
key_facts: The DROP APPLICATION ROLE command removes the specified application role from the system.
The syntax is DROP APPLICATION ROLE [ IF EXISTS ] <name>.
This feature is not supported on Google Cloud Platform.
The command can only be run within the context of an application created using the Native App Framework.
Dropped application roles cannot be recovered and must be recreated within the application.
When dropping an application role from a setup script, the user must ensure that no running version of the application relies upon the role being dropped.
Snowflake recommends either avoiding dropping application roles that may be in use or waiting until the dependent version has also been dropped.
If the identifier contains spaces or special characters, the entire string must be enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
The example DROP APPLICATION ROLE APP_ROLE; drops the application role named APP_ROLE.
The page sits in the Snowflake documentation under APPLICATION, APPLICATION PACKAGE, APPLICATION ROLE, and Additional Commands.
